story.titleZh: “不是朝九晚五的巡航”——从零组建凯迪拉克赛道团队的回报性挑战
story.summaryZh: 凯迪拉克在加入2026年F1赛程前一年开始寻找车队经理，很快锁定了哈斯车队长期任职的车队经理彼得·克罗拉。克罗拉寻求新挑战，并期待再次从零组建团队的机会。
story.originalTitle: "No nine to five cruise" - The rewarding challenge of assembling Cadillac's trackside team from scratch
story.summaryEn: Cadillac began searching for a race team manager a full year before joining the 2026 Formula 1 grid and quickly identified long-serving Haas team manager Peter Crolla. Crolla was looking for a new challenge and saw the chance to build another team from the ground up as the perfect fit.
detailZh: “不是朝九晚五的悠闲差事”——从零组建凯迪拉克赛道车队的艰巨而值得的挑战
车队经理彼得·克罗拉敞开心扉，谈凯迪拉克成为一支受人尊敬的F1车队所经历的艰难历程
当全新加入的凯迪拉克开始寻找一位车队经理时——距离它加入2026年F1发车区还有整整一年——它不必花很长时间、也不必看很远，就锁定了合适的人选。
而在哈斯——F1上一支2016年才起步的车队——长期任职的车队经理彼得·克罗拉正在寻找新的挑战，再次从零开始打造一支车队的机会正合他的心意。
在与格雷姆·洛登进行早期沟通后，克罗拉开始了又一次全新的起点，在九个月的时间里从零开始组建一支赛道边团队。洛登最近被马尔钦·布德科夫斯基取代车队领队一职，但他一直是凯迪拉克在一级方程式中取得体面首秀背后的关键推动力。
"在那个时候，我已经在哈斯车队工作了九年多，我确实准备好迎接改变和新的挑战，我需要一些东西来重新点燃我对这项运动的热情，"克罗拉在最近的一级方程式比利时大奖赛期间、就在车队领导层变动之前告诉Motorsport.com。
"我喜欢组建车队这件事。这会带来巨大的自豪感，而且所有事情都在合适的时机恰好转到了一起。这是我第二次参与新车队的创建，大概间隔了十年，这真的非常棒。做这件事所带来的冲劲、自主权和兴奋感是无与伦比的。
"那九个月大概是我职业生涯中最愉快的时光，从面对一栋空楼和一个计划开始，并被赋予那样的权力去实现你自己的愿景。"
凯迪拉克车队的比赛团队经理彼得·克罗拉（右）与前任领队格雷姆·洛登、技术顾问帕特·西蒙兹以及瓦尔特利·博塔斯
比赛团队经理是一项职责范围极其广泛且多样的工作，首先要负责车队的整体组织事务。当赛事前的后勤工作处理完毕后，一旦赛道上的行动开始，这份工作就会转向更多与竞技相关的角色，其中包括与管理机构国际汽联（FIA）以及F1管理层进行联络。
但从零开始组建一支新车队，为这份工作增添了庞大的基础性层面。克罗拉借鉴了他在哈斯车队的经验，在凯迪拉克再次尝试这样的壮举——考虑到F1新加入者的稀缺性，这是一次非常难得的机会。
“那时候这项运动的面貌非常不同，”克罗拉回顾当年帮助哈斯车队从无到有时说道，“我们还处在伯尼·埃克莱斯顿的时代。规模是一件很重要的事，而且那也是我第一次做这种事，非常令人兴奋。在那段时间里，我和一些很出色的人共事，学到了很多。我认为这为我第二次做这件事打下了良好的基础。”
当被问及在哈斯车队学到的关键经验是什么时，克罗拉回答说：“我认为在那段时间里，赛历和车队所面临的要求都不断增长，我想确保我们以一支大车队的姿态来应对这件事，并且拥有出色完成这项任务所需的一切。
“在我看来，这从来都不是先从小规模做起再逐步壮大的问题。因为没有时间这样做，因为一旦你开始参赛，你能花在各个项目上的时间就会大大减少。所以对我来说，关键在于尽我们所能把每一件事做到最好，充分利用我们可用的预算，打造一支随时可以参赛并把它做好的车队。
“对我来说，这第一年需要有三大支柱。第一是体面地参与比赛。也就是说，我们准时出现在赛场，把所有该做的事情做对，保持低调。我认为我们做到了这一点。第二个支柱是可靠性，可以肯定的是，我们仍在为此努力。第三个是性能，我们也已经进入了这个阶段。所以，一切都在按我的预期进行。到目前为止，一切顺利，我想这么说。
当克罗拉在四月加入时，位于银石的工厂基地已经就绪，但那支将环游世界的赛道团队还只是一张白纸。随后，克罗拉与其他新加入的成员——车队物流经理皮特·西蒙斯和首席机械师内森·迪维——坐下来，共同规划通往墨尔本的道路。这涵盖了从采购车队所需的硬件设备，到为赛道运作、赛车组装、进站换胎等建立流程和最佳实践——对任何车队来说，这都是一份无尽的挑战清单，更不用说一群从未合作过的人了。
“我们采取了协作的方式，对2026年一支优秀车队应该是什么样子有着共同的愿景，”克罗利亚解释道。“没有现成的教科书，也没有关于如何做到这一点的指导方针，但我们非常努力地工作，而且对于我们想做的事情，几乎没有（如果有的话）任何分歧。
“我们只是知道它必须是最好的，但最重要的是，它必须到位。任何东西不到位都是没有借口的，因为我认为在那九个月里一切都是可以实现的，尤其是考虑到我们所拥有的自主权和预算。我们必须给供应商施加很大压力，但我们合作的是之前合作过的好供应商，是我们信任的人，这一点非常重要。知道你可以依靠谁，以及可以把谁真正逼到极限。”
彼得·克罗利亚此前曾在哈斯车队担任类似职务长达十年。
归根结底，任何一个组织都取决于其人员的素质，一级方程式（F1）也不例外，凯迪拉克组建了一支准备挑战既有势力的车队。考虑到其中涉及的漫长“园艺假”（gardening leave，即离职后的强制等待期），这绝非易事，尤其对于一支还没有任何往绩的车队来说更是如此。
“招聘这件事我们必须非常积极，因为人们都已经处于很长的离职通知期了，”克罗拉指出。“在这个行业里，没有人能在少于三个月内真正到岗，有些人甚至有六个月的离职通知期。”
“很多人是在2025年下半年加入的，根本没有什么蜜月期。他们必须立刻投入进去，把所有事情都干起来。每天都有大量的设备运到门口，工作量极其惊人。但每个人都真正迎接了这一挑战。”
不过，正如这种初创文化吸引了克罗拉加入凯迪拉克的故事一样，许多从F1最大车队跳槽过来的其他新员工似乎也有同感。对于车队将面临的挑战，以及绝不会有一帆风顺这回事，大家心里都很清楚。
“不，我认为如果你从一支成熟车队过来，却以为这里会和原来一样，那就是相当被误导了，”克罗拉点头表示。“我认为人们明白更大的图景：加入这样一个项目，它不会是梅赛德斯，也不会是法拉利，那些家伙已经运营了几十年。但与此同时，只要意识到有机会塑造我们自己的环境，我认为人们就看到了其中的吸引力。”
"从其他组织引进人才的关键，在于认清他们的优势、认清他们的经验，并把这些挖掘出来，打造我们共同的工作流程。从其他车队来到比赛团队和更广泛业务的申请者的质量和数量都非常令人振奋。但这需要一种能够迎接挑战的心态。这不会是一份朝九晚五的轻松工作。而是要深挖潜力，做好长期奋斗的准备。"
"我们所做的一切都没有超出我的预期。我原以为可能会更难一些，也可能以为在某些时候会更令人失望。"——克罗拉。
凯迪拉克在此过程中确实按时完成了每一项内部和外部期限，顺利开始了冬季测试，并在澳大利亚用其中一辆赛车完成了首场比赛。但随后在可靠性和运营方面出现的小毛病，加上在队尾被阿斯顿·马丁超越，进一步表明仅仅参赛只是起点。
"这些里程碑并不容易达成。每一个里程碑背后都真真切切地凝聚着血、汗和泪，"克罗拉回顾道，"它真的会变成你的生活。它必须如此，因为你每天要工作超长时间，还要求其他所有人也同样付出。我认为没有任何其他运动能像这样，当你真正造出一辆赛车并让它第一次驶上赛道时，能亲眼看到自己劳动的成果。那也许只是一个一月里银石赛道阴冷下雨的下午，但那感觉太棒了。它给了所有人一种巨大的成就感。
"毫无疑问，我们遇到了可靠性方面的问题。我认为这对任何人来说都不意外，但关键在于你如何面对它们、如何解决它们、以及如何从中恢复。对我来说，我们所做的一切与我预期的情况并没有脱节。我可能原本预计会更艰难一些，有时也可能预计会更令人失望一些。奥地利站大概算是我们的一个低谷，但这只是旅程的一部分。如果有人对此感到惊讶，那么我认为对我们来说经历这一切可能是一次有益的经验。"
随着凯迪拉克进入下一个阶段，前雷诺人士布德科夫斯基如今执掌车队，车队明年将开始启用位于印第安纳州费舍尔市的全新美国总部，克罗拉坚称那里将是一个"绝佳的运营基地"，同时在未来几个月里还将扩建位于银石赛道的英国基地。
"开始参赛并不是建设和发展这项事业的终点。它其实只是这段旅程中的又一个阶段，我认为要等到所有这些各自独立的部门都全面运转起来，我们才能真正看清我们在这里所做之事的规模，"他补充道。
"这里有一些非常有才华的人才，不过于自夸地说，我们做得不错，但我们才刚刚起步。"
detailEn: "No nine to five cruise" - The rewarding challenge of assembling Cadillac's trackside team from scratch
Race team manager Peter Crolla opens up on Cadillac's challenging journey to becoming a respected Formula 1 team

When brand-new entrant Cadillac started its search for a race team manager, still a full year removed from joining the 2026 Formula 1 grid, it didn't have to look very long, or far, to identify the right target.

Over at Haas, F1's previous start-up team in 2016, long serving team manager Peter Crolla had been looking for a new challenge, and the prospect of another chance to build a team from the ground up was ticking all the right boxes.

Following early conversations with Graeme Lowdon, who was recently replaced by Marcin Budkowski as team principal but has been the instrumental driving force behind Cadillac's respectable F1 debut, Crolla embarked on another fresh start building up a trackside team from scratch over a nine-month period.

"I'd been at Haas for over nine years at that point, and I was definitely ready for a change and a new challenge, and I needed something to get my excitement back for the sport," Crolla old Motorsport.com at the recent Belgian Grand Prix, before the team's leadership change.

"I love the element of setting up a team. There's a great deal of pride in that, and everything just aligned at the right time. It's my second new team start, sort of 10 years apart, and it was absolutely brilliant. The momentum, the autonomy and the excitement of doing that is unparalleled.
"That nine month period was probably the most enjoyable of my career, from starting with an empty building and a plan, and being given that authority to create your vision."
Cadillac race team manager Peter Crolla (right) with former team principal Graeme Lowdon, technical consultant Pat Symonds and Valtteri Bottas

Being a race team manager in a job with an extremely wide and diverse scope, starts with being responsible for the overall organisation of the race team. Once the pre-event logistics are out of the way, the job then shifts into a more sporting oriented role when the on-track action starts, which includes liaising with governing body the FIA and F1 management.

But starting a new team from zero adds a huge foundational layer to that, with Crolla drawing from his experience at Haas to have another go at Cadillac, which is a very rare opportunity in F1 given the scarcity of new entrants.

"The sport was a very different place back then," Crolla said, looking back on helping bring Haas to life. "We were still in the Bernie Ecclestone era. Scale was a big thing, and it was also my first time doing it. It was exciting. I worked with some great people there during that period, and learnt a lot. And I think that set me up well for doing it the second time round."

When asked what his key lessons were from Haas, Crolla replied: "I think the calendar and the requirements on a team have grown over the course of that period, and I wanted to ensure that we approached this as a big team and had everything we needed to accomplish the task well.

"It was, in my opinion, never a case of starting small and then growing. There isn't time for that because once you're out racing, the time you've got to spend on your projects is greatly decreased. So for me, it was about doing everything to the best of our abilities, maximising the budget we had available for it, and just creating a team that was ready to go racing and do a good job of it.

"For me, there were three pillars of how this first year needed to be. It was respectable participation. So, we show up on time, and we do all the right things, keep our heads down. I think we accomplished that. The next pillar was reliability, and for sure we're still working our way through that. And then the third is performance, and we're into that phase as well. So, it's happening as I thought it would. So far so good. I would say."

While the factory-based operation in Silverstone was already in place when Crolla joined in April, the trackside team that would travel the world was still a blank sheet of paper. Crolla subsequently sat down with fellow new hires, team logistics manager Pete Simmons and chief mechanic Nathan Divey, to map out the road to Melbourne. That ranged from acquiring the hardware the team needed to setting up procedures and best practices for trackside operations, car builds, pitstops - an endless list of challenges for any outfit, never mind a team of people that had never worked together before.

"We had a collaborative approach and a collective vision of what a good race team in 2026 needed to look like," Crolla explained. "There's no book. There are no guidelines on how to do this, but we worked very hard and there were very few, if any, disagreements on what we wanted to do.

"We just knew that it had to be the best, but most of all, it had to be there. There were no excuses for anything not being there because I think everything is achievable in those nine months, and especially given the autonomy and the budget we had. We had to put a lot of pressure on suppliers, but we worked with good suppliers that we'd worked with before. People that we trusted, and that was really important. Knowing who you can lean on and who you can really push to the limit."
Peter Crolla previously spent a decade at Haas in a similar role.

Ultimately, any organisation comes down to the quality of its people, and F1 is no different as Cadillac assembled a team ready to take on the establishment. Given the long gardening leave times involved, that was no easy feat, especially for a team that had no track record yet.

"Recruitment was something that we had to be quite aggressive on because people were already on long notice periods," Crolla pointed out. "Nobody's really available in this sport for any less than three months, and some were on six months' notice.

"A lot of people joined in the second half of 2025, and there was no honeymoon period. They had to get stuck in right away and get on with it all. There was a huge amount of equipment coming through the door every day, and a phenomenal workload. But everybody really rose to the challenge."

But just like how the start-up culture attracted Crolla to the Cadillac story, a lot of other hires from F1's biggest teams appeared to feel the same way. There was certainly no mistake on the challenges the team would face, and that there would be no such thing as an easy ride.

"No, I think that would be quite misguided if you came here from an established team and thought it was just going to be like that," Crolla nodded. "I think people understand the bigger picture that coming to a project like this, it's not going to be a Mercedes. It's not going to be a Ferrari where these guys have been in operation for decades. But at the same time, just recognising the opportunity of sculpting our own environment, I think people saw the attraction in that.

"The important part of bringing people in from other organisations is recognising their strengths, recognising their experience, and drawing that out of them to create our combined processes. The quality and quantity of applicants that came into the race team and the wider business from other teams has been really positive. But it needs that mentality that can rise to the challenge. This is not going to be a nine to five cruise. It's digging deep and being in it for the long run."

"Nothing that we've done is out of sync with how I expected it to be. I probably expected it to be a little bit harder, and probably expected it to be a little bit more disappointing at times." - Crolla.

Cadillac did meet every internal and external deadline along the way, making the start of winter testing and finishing its first race in Australia with one of its cars. But subsequent gremlins on the reliability and operational side, while being overtaken by Aston Martin at the rear of the field, have further underlined that simply showing up was just the start.

"Those were not easy milestones to reach. There was literally blood, sweat, and tears for all of them," Crolla reflected. "It turns into your life, really. It has to, because you're working super long days and you're asking everybody else to do the same. I think there's no greater sport where you're able to see the fruits of your labour when you actually build a car that then goes around the track for the first time. It might have been on a rainy cold afternoon in January in Silverstone, but it was mega. It gave everybody a great feeling of achievement.

"For sure, we've come across reliability matters. I don't think that was a surprise to anybody, but it's about how you approach them, how you tackle them, and how you recover from them. For me, nothing that we've done is out of sync with how I expected it to be. I probably expected it to be a little bit harder, and probably expected it to be a little bit more disappointing at times. Austria was probably a bit of a low point for us, but it's just part of the journey. If people were surprised by it, then I think it's probably a useful experience for us to go through."

As Cadillac transitions into its next phase, with former Renault man Budkowski now at the helm, the team will start using a brand-new US headquarters in Fishers, Indiana next year that Crolla insists will be an "amazing place to operate from", while also expanding its UK base in Silverstone in the coming months.

"Starting to go racing is not the end point of building and developing the business. It's really just another stage in that journey, and I think it won't be until all these discrete areas are fully operational that we actually see the scale of what we're doing here," he added.
"There's some really talented people here, and without being overly congratulatory on ourselves, we're doing a good job with it, but we're only just getting started."

detailZh: 迈凯伦如何缓解拉斯维加斯F1直道速度劣势
由于兰多·诺里斯和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里的最高速度不足，这对迈凯伦车手不得不充分利用拉斯维加斯的赛道位置博弈
奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，迈凯伦，兰多·诺里斯，迈凯伦
尽管在这条放大了MCL40缺陷而不奖励其优点的赛道上取得了还算体面的成绩，兰多·诺里斯对拉斯维加斯大奖赛周末周五的表现并不满意。
“我们在直道上简直太糟糕了，”诺里斯在排位赛获得第五名后不久说道，他落后杆位得主基米·安东内利近0.8秒，后者因引擎罚单将退后五位，使诺里斯在发车格上升至第四。
长直道和低下压力需求意味着拉斯维加斯大道赛道从来不会成为这辆赛车最强的赛道，正如迈凯伦在蒙扎和巴库这两个最接近的对比赛道上表现平淡所预示的那样。
但迈凯伦在拉斯维加斯的差距仍然大得令人惊讶，至少对安东内利来说是这样，诺里斯和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里在拉斯维加斯大道的长直道以及通往终点的最后一段直道上通常都慢了20公里/小时。
如此巨大的差异很少仅仅归因于单一因素，周五的情况也证明了这一点。尽管有定期升级，MCL40仍然相对阻力较大且空气动力学效率不高，而车队在季前选择采用更短的传动比，使其在拥有极长直道的赛道上损失了最高速的爆发力。
与所有车队一样，迈凯伦本可以选择在赛季中期对齿轮比进行一次调整，但最终决定不这么做，因为其较短的齿比在其他赛道上仍然能带来优势。然而在拉斯维加斯，车队不得不为此付出代价。

当被 Motorsport.com 问及车队的劣势是否比预期更严重时，车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉回答说：“我们确实有些担心这条赛道的要求对我们的赛车有多适合。这不仅仅是最高速度的问题，还涉及最高速度与大家都在努力利用的尾流效应的结合。因此，你会进入发动机在某些工况下的运转状态，而用我们的齿比来说并不理想。我们知道从空气动力学角度来看，阻力并不是我们的强项。我们看到了与蒙扎、巴库相似的特征。而在所有条件下，我们都不是特别有竞争力。”
由于尾流效应如此关键——这一点从主导第三节排位赛并让伊萨克·哈贾尔和乔治·拉塞尔等人付出代价的位置战术中可见一斑——迈凯伦试图通过更积极地追逐尾流来弥补最高速度的不足。
斯特拉补充说：“我们在这里做得更好的是通过非常好的位置安排来缓解这一问题。在排位赛中，赛车几乎处于我们想要的位置。这确实有帮助。因为我必须说，在这些规则下，当你跟随一辆甚至多辆赛车时，阻力减少似乎比过去更多。因此，处于正确位置的激励甚至更高。”
诺里斯详细解释道：“我必须在距离前车1.5秒的地方开始我的飞驰圈，这意味着在每个弯道我至少会损失半成到一成的时间，因为我损失的了下压力太多了。显然，最终拥有一个好的尾流会带来更大的收益，但我们不得不弥补直线速度的严重损失——因此我们必须牺牲我们的过弯速度。”
再加上外部因素，安东内利在小红牛和阿尔派车队的一群赛车末尾获得了“极端”的尾流，迈凯伦的真实差距可能被夸大了。两位车手在直道上损失的时间远不及安东内利的队友乔治·拉塞尔，也不及马克斯·维斯塔潘——后者将在周六因安东内利五位的发车位罚退而继承杆位。
尽管如此，皮亚斯特里认为迈凯伦最高速度劣势的幅度比预期更大，不过他也承认自己第七快的成绩是一圈混乱的飞驰圈所致。“说实话，这让我们感到意外，”这位澳大利亚车手说。“我认为我们没料到这会是个这么大的问题。在蒙扎我们还行，对我们来说奇怪的是，这主要是与其他梅赛德斯动力赛车相比。”
“我认为有几件事我们可能会复盘，看看能否做得稍微好一点。但我觉得我的圈速也有点混乱。”
斯特拉对迈凯伦修改后的底板持乐观态度，该底板由诺里斯在维加斯试用，并帮助提升了低速性能，但这位意大利人透露了一个不寻常的原因，说明为何该升级的性能收益在很大程度上被抵消了。
“在兰多这边，一个塑料袋卡在了底板里，我们在那里损失了相当多的下压力。所以，考虑到十分之一秒就会带来很大差别，那个塑料袋上肯定有十分之一秒的损失，这有点可惜。
“但现在我们需要研究如何在正赛中保持赛车的可比赛性。在蒙扎我们看到，由于这种尾流效应，你实际上可以保持纠缠、与其他赛车相连。所以我们肯定期待明天，并且排位赛一直很有竞争力这一事实令我们感到鼓舞。”
detailEn: How McLaren tried to mitigate its Las Vegas F1 top speed deficit
With Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri down on top speed, the McLaren pair had to make the most of Las Vegas's track position games
Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Lando Norris, McLaren

Despite what was a respectable result on a circuit that accentuated the MCL40's flaws without rewarding its virtues, Lando Norris was not best pleased with how Friday at the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend.

“We're just shocking on the straights,” said Norris shortly after qualifying fifth, just under eight tenths behind polesitter Kimi Antonelli, who is set to drop five places for an engine penalty, elevating Norris to fourth on the grid.

The long straights and low downforce demands meant the Las Vegas Strip circuit was never going to be the strongest track for this car, as foreshadowed by McLaren's muted form on the circuit's nearest comparisons in Monza and Baku.

But McLaren's deficit in Vegas was still surprisingly vast, at least to Antonelli, with Norris and Oscar Piastri routinely 20km/h down on the circuit's long Las Vegas Boulevard as well as the final straight towards the finish.

Differences so massive are rarely just down to one single factor, and that also proved to be the case on Friday. Despite regular upgrades, the MCL40 remains relatively draggy and aerodynamically inefficient, which is compounded by the team's pre-season choice to go for a shorter gearing, costing it top-end grunt on circuits with extremely long straights.

Like all teams, McLaren had the option to make one mid-season change to its gear ratios, but decided against it because its shorter gearing would still stand it in good stead on other circuits. In Vegas, though, the team had to pay the price.

"Definitely we had some concern in terms of how suitable the demands of this circuit would be for our car," team principal Andrea Stella replied when asked by Motorsport.com whether the squad's deficit was more severe than anticipated. "This is not only the top speed, it is also the top speed that is combined with the towing that everyone is trying to do. So, you go in operating regimes of the engine that with our ratios is not ideal. We know that the drag from an aerodynamic point of view is not a point of strength. We have seen traits that are similar to Monza, to Baku. And in all conditions we were not particularly competitive."

With slipstreaming so crucial, as evidenced by the positional tactics that dominated Q3 and cost the likes of Isack Hadjar and George Russell, McLaren tried to compensate for its lack of top speed by more aggressively chasing the tow.

"What we have done better here is to mitigate this by having really good positioning," Stella added. "The car was pretty much where we wanted it to be in qualifying. And this definitely helped. Because I have to say that it seems like with these regulations the drag reduction when you follow one car or even multiple cars is more than in the past. And therefore, there is an even higher incentive to be positioned in the right place."

Norris elaborated: “I have to start my lap 1.5 seconds off the car ahead, which means in every corner I'm losing at least half a tenth to a tenth, because of how much downforce I'm losing. There's obviously a bigger gain at the end of the day in having a good slipstream, but we're having to make up for a really terrible loss of straight-line speed - and therefore we have to harm our cornering speed."

Add in the external factor of Antonelli receiving an "extreme" tow at the end of a gaggle of cars from Racing Bulls and Alpine, and McLaren's real deficit has probably been exaggerated. Neither driver lost nearly as much time on the straights to Antonelli's team-mate George Russell or indeed Max Verstapppen, who will inherit pole on Saturday due to Antonelli's five-place grid penalty.

Still, Piastri felt the size of McLaren's top speed disadvantage was bigger than expected, though he also admitted his seventh-fastest time was the result of a messy lap. "t caught us by surprise, to be honest," the Australian said. "I don't think we expected it to be such a big problem. At Monza we were okay and the strange part for us is it's mostly compared to the other Mercedes-powered cars.
"I think there were a few things that we probably will review and see if we can do a slightly better job. But I think also my laps were a little bit messy."

Stella was upbeat about McLaren's revised floor which was trialled by Norris in Vegas and helped low-speed performance, but the Italian revealed an unusual reason why that upgrade's performance benefit was largely cancelled out.

"On Lando's side, a plastic bag got stuck in the floor and we lost quite a lot of downforce there. So, considering that one tenth of a second would make a big difference, certainly there was one tenth of a second on a plastic bag, which is a bit of a shame.

"But now we need to look at how we keep the car raceable in the race. At Monza we saw that because of this towing effect you actually can stay tangled, linked to the other cars. So we are definitely looking forward to tomorrow and encouraged by the fact that qualifying has been competitive."

relatedItems.originalTitle: Kimi Antonelli and George Russell set for Mercedes talks over Las Vegas GP qualifying woes
detailZh: 基米·安东内利和乔治·拉塞尔将就拉斯维加斯大奖赛排位赛的困境与梅赛德斯进行会谈
安东内利在拉斯维加斯的排位赛中速度最快，拉塞尔排名第三，但他们的策略并未按计划进行
安德烈亚·基米·安东内利、梅赛德斯、乔治·拉塞尔、梅赛德斯
乔治·拉塞尔和基米·安东内利将在团队指令和赛道位置出现混乱后，就一级方程式拉斯维加斯大奖赛排位赛的后果进行“线下”讨论。
周五晚上的排位赛中，交通状况扮演了重要角色，车手们不愿意第一个出发，因为在这个低下压力的街道赛赛道上，被拖曳的优势很大。
由于有五位车手需要接受发车位处罚，他们的主要任务是帮助队友，比如哈斯车队的奥利弗·贝尔曼在Q1中给拉斐尔·卡马拉提供拖曳。
安东内利也是其中之一，因为更换新引擎被降了五位发车位，所以计划是在争夺杆位的比赛中给拉塞尔提供尾流，但很快计划就破产了。
这是因为梅赛德斯车队的双雄在最后一圈被夹在阿尔卑斯车队和小红牛车队之间，尽管试图寻找空间，但有时却不得不进行三车并排。
安东内利最终在5号弯道减速，而拉塞尔不情愿地成为车队的领跑者，2026年的世界冠军在排位赛中速度最快，他的队友落后0.331秒排在第三。
当被问及之后是否希望得到安东内利的帮助时，拉塞尔回答说：“如果你有发车罚分，尽可能从更高的位置起步仍然很重要。”
“但我们会私下讨论这个问题。我认为明天的比赛将非常接近，就像蒙扎一样——要想从车队中脱颖而出将非常具有挑战性。”
“我本希望站在杆位，但我认为只要在顶尖的前七名位置，你就有机会竞争。”
这种情况让梅赛德斯车队老板Toto Wolff对安东内利能最快感到难以置信，尤其是因为拉塞尔没有得到他离开维修区第二位的请求。
“这非常危险，”拉塞尔补充道，他将与红牛车队的马克斯·维斯塔潘一起占据前排，因为安东内利的处罚。
“基米获得了杆位，但如果他晚出发一秒，他就无法完成这一圈了。
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，乔治·拉塞尔，梅赛德斯
“因为每个人都想要这么做，而且有一半的赛车在做准备圈，另一半的赛车没有，这也使得事情变得很困难。”
“如果你可以选择，你会在九辆车的一组中排在最后，大约有3秒的差距，如果你能完美选择的话。”
“但这就是每个人都追求的，所以这有点像2019年的蒙扎。”
“尽管安东内利最终退后给了他设置最快圈速所需的空间，1分33.893秒，但这可能让他付出了代价，因为他刚好及时冲过终点线开始最后一圈。”
“正如乔治所说，我们会讨论这件事，因为我们总是在排位赛中被派到前面，”安东内利说。
“关于5号弯，这完全是我的责任。就像我说的，我们一开始就是三车并排，我只是说，'你知道什么？我要减速。'”，
“这很棘手，首先，我差点错过了旗帜。是的，我确实受到了很大的牵引，但我离得太近，以至于在脏空气中等情况下绕过弯角实际上很困难。”
“我们已经使用了低下压力套件，所以当你跟车时，你更能感觉到损失。”
“但总的来说，这只是那种你认为你完了，但实际上却成功了的情况。”
“在第五弯道，我决定减速。我并不真的知道我的时间安排有多紧张。我可能本会做得不同，但事后看来，结果仍然不错。”
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli and George Russell set for Mercedes talks over Las Vegas GP qualifying woes
Antonelli was fastest in qualifying at Las Vegas with Russell third, but their strategy did not go as planned
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes
George Russell and Kimi Antonelli will discuss the fallout from Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying “offline” following confusion over team orders and track position.
Traffic played a significant role in qualifying on Friday night with drivers reluctant to go first, considering the advantage of a tow is huge around the low-downforce street circuit.
There was the added complexity of five drivers taking a grid penalty, so their primary role was to help their team-mate like Haas’ Oliver Bearman giving Rafael Camara a tow in Q1.
Antonelli was another one of those, taking a five-place drop for a new engine, so the plan was to give Russell the slipstream in the fight for pole but it quickly unravelled.
That was because the Mercedes duo got caught in a pack with both Alpine and Racing Bulls cars ahead of the final lap, at times going three-wide despite trying to find space.
Antonelli eventually backed off at Turn 5 while Russell reluctantly went first of the pack and the 2026 world champion was fastest in qualifying with his team-mate 0.331s off in third.
So when asked afterwards if he was hoping for assistance from Antonelli, Russell replied: “It's still important, if you've got a grid penalty, to start as high up the order as possible.
“But we'll take it offline and we can talk about it. I think tomorrow is going to be very close between everybody, similar to Monza - it'll be very challenging to pull away from the pack.
“I would have liked to have been on pole, but I think anywhere in the top seven positions and you're in the fight.”
The situation caused Mercedes boss Toto Wolff to express disbelief at how Antonelli was quickest, particularly because Russell didn’t receive his request of leaving the pits second.
“It's very high risk,” added Russell, who will share the front row with Red Bull’s Max Verstappen due to Antonelli’s penalty.
“Kimi got the pole, but if he started the lap a second later, he wouldn't have got the lap in.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes
“It's very difficult to orchestrate because everybody's going for it, and also the fact that half the cars were doing prep laps and half the cars were not also made it difficult.
“If you could choose, you would be at the back of a pack of nine cars with around a three-second gap, if you could perfectly choose.
“But that's what everyone's chasing, so it's kind of like Monza 2019."
Although Antonelli eventually backing off gave him the space needed to set his fastest lap, a 1m33.893s, it could have cost him as he only just crossed the line in time to start his final tour.
“As George said, we will talk about it because we've been sent out at the front in qualifying always,” said Antonelli.
“About Turn 5, it was fully on me. Like I said, we were three-wide, first of all, and I just said, "You know what? I'm just going to back off’."
“It was tricky because, first of all, I almost missed the flag. Yes, I did get a big tow, but I was also so close that getting around the corner was actually difficult with the dirty air and so on.
“We're already on a lower-downforce package, so you do feel even more the loss when following.
“But overall, it was just one of those times where you think you're screwed, but actually it works out.
“On Turn 5, I just decided to back off. I didn't really know how tight I was with the timing. I probably would have done it differently, but in hindsight, it still worked out.”

relatedItems.originalTitle: Max Verstappen shares theory on Ferrari's lack of top speed in F1 2026
detailZh: 维斯塔潘分享对法拉利F1 2026速度不足的理论
除了较小的涡轮，维斯塔潘还指出法拉利的"排气吹拂"问题。在拉斯维加斯这样的赛道上，速度不足尤为明显。
尽管维斯塔潘对他在拉斯维加斯大奖赛排位赛中第二快的时间并不满意，指出小红牛22存在神秘问题，但观察法拉利的情况显示情况可能更加糟糕。
自2025年伊莫拉以来，法拉利车队首次在Q2阶段两辆赛车都被淘汰，之后刘易斯·汉密尔顿解释说地板损坏和部署问题阻碍了他。他估计缺失的地板部分让他失去了三到四十分之一秒，而部署问题又让他失去了另外六十分之一秒。
尽管如此，法拉利事先就已经知道拉斯维加斯赛道对SF-26来说将是一个相当大的挑战。这部分原因与有意的工程设计选择有关。法拉利使用的涡轮比大多数其他动力单元制造商都要小，这使得位于马拉内洛的法拉利车队在起步时具有优势，尤其是在今年年初，但也对整体动力产生了影响。
法拉利获得了两个ADUO代币，这意味着根据国际汽联的测量，这家意大利制造商在最佳内燃机引擎上落后了2%到4%，而红牛的引擎就是最佳内燃机引擎。
在拉斯维加斯，这一点尤其痛苦，因为当导流板在长直道上启动时，F1车手必须完全依赖内燃机的动力在一定时间内行驶。
这解释了为什么法拉利在最高速度上如此缺乏动力，尽管维斯塔潘看到了另一个影响因素。
“他们显然缺乏顶级速度，但这与他们的排气吹拂设计方式有关。因为如果你看看哈斯，直道上这个问题要小得多，”当Motorsport.com问他关于法拉利灾难性的排位赛时，维斯塔潘说。
“这始终是你要多少下压力和愿意为此牺牲多少动力的结合。你把排气前面的那个东西做得越大，你失去的动力就越多。所以从某种程度上说，这显然也在他们自己的掌控之中。”
维斯塔潘指的是法拉利的排气翼，这是斯库德里亚今年开创的概念。它有助于产生额外的下压力，但维斯塔潘认为它也可能成为拉斯维加斯等赛道长直道上的额外障碍。
“在这样的赛道上，这确实可能是一个大障碍。所以你可能需要稍微适应一下，但这显然是他们自己必须解决的问题！”
红牛车队在能源匮乏的赛道上取得了显著的进步。在今年年初，这类赛场的效率仍然是我们的弱点，尤其是与梅赛德斯相比，但红牛福特动力系统在整个赛季中在该领域获得了大量的知识。
"一开始，我们的赛车显然有很多问题，而且在动力单元方面也没有完全掌握。我认为这自动意味着我们有一些更容易的步骤要走，但我们仍然完成了这些步骤。这是我们值得骄傲的事情。"
除了纯粹的性能之外，执行也是拉斯维加斯的一个主要因素。尾流产生了极端的影响，许多车手表示，这甚至比他们之前经历过的任何事情都要大，这使得法拉利车手在排位赛中大部分时间没有尾流显得更加令人惊讶。
考虑到他们缺乏最高速度，这似乎是一种奇怪的方法，尽管维斯塔潘不愿意在这方面对法拉利过于苛刻。
“嗯，这是从外面看的。我只专注于我们自己的车队。当然，我们的目标始终是尽可能少犯错误，尽可能多地掌握一切。我认为我们在今天的执行方面做得相当不错。”
detailEn: Max Verstappen shares theory on Ferrari's lack of top speed in F1 2026
Besides the smaller turbo, Verstappen also points to Ferrari's "exhaust blowing". The lack of top speed is particularly painful at a circuit like Las Vegas

Although Max Verstappen was not entirely satisfied with his second-fastest time in qualifying for the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix – pointing to a mysterious issue with the RB22 – a glance at Ferrari shows that things could have been considerably worse.

For the first time since Imola 2025, the Scuderia saw both cars eliminated in Q2, after which Lewis Hamilton explained that floor damage and deployment issues had hampered him. He estimated that the missing section of the floor had cost him three to four tenths, while the deployment issue had cost him another six tenths.

That said, Ferrari already knew beforehand that the Las Vegas circuit would pose a considerable challenge for the SF-26. This is partly related to deliberate design choices. Ferrari runs a smaller turbo than most other power unit manufacturers, which gave the Maranello-based team an advantage off the line, particularly at the start of this year, but also has implications for outright power.

Ferrari has received two ADUO tokens, meaning that, according to FIA measurements, the Italian manufacturer was between 2% and 4% down on the best internal combustion engine on the grid, Red Bull's unit.
In Las Vegas, that is particularly painful, as clipping kicks in on the long straight and F1 drivers then have to rely solely on the internal combustion engine's power for a certain period.
This partly explains why Ferrari is lacking so much top speed, although Verstappen sees another contributing factor.

"They are obviously lacking top speed, but that has to do with the way they have designed their exhaust blowing as well. Because if you look at Haas, it's much less of an issue on the straight," Verstappen said when Motorsport.com asked him about Ferrari's disastrous qualifying session.

"It's always a combination of how much downforce you want to have and how much power you're willing to sacrifice for it. The bigger you make that thing in front of the exhaust, the more power you lose. So to some extent, it's obviously in their own hands as well."

Verstappen is referring to Ferrari's exhaust wing, a concept the Scuderia has pioneered this year. It helps generate additional downforce, but Verstappen believes it can also become an extra handicap on the long straights of tracks such as Las Vegas.
"At a circuit like this, it can indeed be a major handicap. So perhaps you have to adapt a little to that, but that's obviously something they have to figure out for themselves!"

Red Bull, meanwhile, has made significant strides on energy-poor circuits. At the start of this year, efficiency at such venues was still a weakness, particularly compared to Mercedes, but Red Bull Ford Powertrains has gained a great deal of knowledge in that area over the course of the season.

"At the beginning, we obviously had a lot of problems with our car and we weren't quite on top of things with the power unit either. I think that automatically meant we had some easier steps to make, but we still made those steps. And that's something we should be proud of."

Aside from outright performance, execution is also a major factor in Las Vegas. The slipstream had an extreme effect, with many drivers saying it was even greater than anything they had experienced before, making it all the more surprising that the Ferrari drivers were mostly without a slipstream during qualifying.
Particularly given their lack of top speed, that seems a strange approach, although Verstappen preferred not to be too critical of Ferrari in that respect.

"Well, that's judging from the outside. I just focus on our own team. Of course, our goal is always to make as few mistakes as possible and to stay on top of everything as much as we can. I think we did a pretty good job in terms of execution today."

keyPointsEn: Verstappen points out that the reasons for Ferrari's lack of top speed include a smaller turbo and 'exhaust blowing' issues.
The lack of top speed is particularly noticeable at circuits like Las Vegas.
For the first time since Imola 2025, both Ferrari cars were eliminated in Q2.
